conviction_note: The one big new fact (the AST SpaceMobile engine and licence deal of 2026-11-06, over $1.3bn) is already in the tape: the stock is up about 54% from its 2026-11-05 one-year-low close of $15.18 to $23.37. That leaves a probable revenue beat against a disputed bar, on a name whose last 34% revenue beat bought +0.68%, set against a crowded run-up and an Alpha Flight 8 that has still not flown. Findings sum to -1.5. The scaled number, p_up 47 x abs 11, gives -0.66; the two agree in sign and the gap is the wide two-way tail (a guide raise on the licence, or sell-the-news).

Company FY2026 guide is $420-450M revenue (reiterated 2026-08-11, with 95% of the midpoint booked), and FY consensus is about $440M. Because the quarterly bar has disagreeing sources, findings that depend on it are capped small.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue is likely to beat the $106.3M consensus. Q2 revenue was $117.7M (spacecraft $108.3M, launch $9.4M). Management said 95% of the $435M FY midpoint was already booked. With H1 at about $199M, the guide midpoint implies about $118M a quarter in H2, so the consensus models a sequential drop to $106M. Q2 itself beat the street ($88.7M) by about 34%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-11): a revenue beat of about 34% with the guide reiterated, and the stock moved +0.68%. Q1 2026 (2026-05-04): -5.54%. Q3 2025 (2025-11-12): +16.99% on a revenue beat. Beats have been bought little recently.
findings.source: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/firefly-aerospace-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-11/ (summarised via search; the page itself returned 403) and https://runtimewire.com/article/firefly-aerospace-hits-record-117-7m-q2-revenue-beating-estimates-by-34
findings.why_not_priced: If the street had priced a flat-to-up Q3, consensus would sit near $115-118M rather than $106M. One aggregated figure of $114.56M suggests some estimates have moved up, which is why this is capped small. The 54% run since 2026-11-05 is about the AST deal, not the Q3 line.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/FLY/22738 (2026-11-03) has the arithmetic: consensus implies a record Q4 near $135M, so the street has back-loaded the year. It shares the Q2 figures with the source.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide could be raised because of the AST licence. Reported terms are about $800M for a perpetual manufacturing licence, $400M of it in cash plus 10-14M ASTS Class A shares, alongside $250M of engines and $250M of engineering over three years. If the licence is a distinct performance obligation transferred at a point in time, part of it could be booked in Q4 2026 and lift the $420-450M range well above consensus. Management will have to address this on the 2026-11-10 call. This is an accounting inference: no filing yet states the recognition.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide was reiterated in March, May and August 2026, so the last raises predate this window. Benzinga's tracker says guidance was raised twice over its period. The +16.99% move on 2025-11-12 came with strong guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: The rally priced the deal's existence and the backlog. No article found discusses recognition timing or a guidance effect (Trefis 2026-11-07 says only that 'backlog is the key figure to watch'). If the market expected a licence-driven raise to the FY guide, the sell-side would have published pro-forma FY26 numbers. None was found, and the one tracker found showed no upward estimate revisions in the last month.
findings.independence: CBS Austin https://cbsaustin.com/news/local/firefly-to-supply-engines-for-ast-spacemobile-rocket-in-13b-deal (2026-11-06) confirms the $800M/$250M/$250M split and the perpetual licence. EDGAR shows no Firefly 8-K for the deal as of the fetch (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001860160.json), so the terms are not in a company filing. The recognition is my inference.

findings.finding: The AST deal has not yet been put into any Firefly filing. The Q3 release and 10-Q (subsequent events, remaining performance obligations) are the first company documents that can quantify it: backlog of $1.5bn at 2026-06-30 against a deal worth nearly as much, plus the timing of the $400M cash, which would cover about four quarters of the -$106M free cash flow.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The record $1.5bn backlog on 2026-08-11 bought +0.68%. The deal announcement itself moved the stock +36.8% on 2026-11-06.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the deal value is public and the stock re-rated 54%. What is unpriced is the cash schedule and its effect on dilution risk. On 2026-11-03 the stock was being discussed with $940M liquidity against a -$106M a quarter burn. If the market had priced the funding as settled, the stock would not still be 60% below its high with 180% IV.
findings.independence: Shares deal facts with findings 2 and 4. Liquidity and burn come from the Q2 release via https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/FLY/22738.

findings.finding: The stock runs into the print up 37.35% over five days and about 54% from the 2026-11-05 close of $15.18 (a one-year low), on deal news rather than on Q3. A print that only confirms the guide risks sell-the-news. This is sized down for short interest near 17% of float with 3.2 days to cover (Sep 30), which may not be fully covered, and for an option market paying for upside (skew -4.15).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: a big beat into a weak tape bought +0.68%. 2026-05-04: -5.54%. No prior print came on a comparable five-day run-up.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up is the price, and the skew does not lean down, so the market is not positioned for a give-back. That is the case for the finding, and also why it is small: the option market disagrees.
findings.independence: The baseline tape (run_up_5d 37.35%, spot 23.37) is independent of the Trefis close data. Short interest is from https://massive.com/quote/fly and points the other way.

findings.finding: 11,111,116 SciTec merger shares have been freely saleable under Rule 144 since 2026-10-31. Firefly filed a POS AM on 2026-11-02 ending the resale registration. Those holders can sell into a 54% rally around the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior unlock coincided with a print. The share count is about 7% of roughly 160M outstanding and about 16% of a roughly 70M float.
findings.why_not_priced: The filing is a termination post-effective amendment that no news item carried. If supply were priced, the rally would have stalled on heavy volume; that cannot be checked from here.

findings.finding: Alpha Flight 8, the Block II debut, has still not flown. In August management promised the next two Alpha launches in Q4 2026, after cutting the year from four launches to three. No launch date had been announced by 2026-11-10, so a slip of at least one launch into 2027 is likely and only one Alpha flew in 2026 (Flight 7, March). Launch is about 8% of revenue ($9.4M of $117.7M in Q2), so the revenue effect is small; the damage is to credibility and to the Eclipse/Miranda narrative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The slip to Q4 was announced on 2026-08-11 and the stock moved +0.68%. A booster explosion on 2025-09-29 cost about -24%. A slip on its own has been absorbed.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the preview frames Q4 around the delayed launch. A further slip into 2027 has not been confirmed by the company. If it were priced, the guide's low end would be the street's FY number rather than $440M.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/FLY/22738 (2026-11-03) says Flight 8 has slipped with no firm date. The rest of the company: spacecraft (92% of Q2) is booked, so revenue is net-protected.

findings.finding: Gross margin fell from 27.7% to 20.3% over the two quarters to Q2, which management attributed to FORGE hardware purchases, and free cash flow widened to -$106.3M (including a roughly $24M SciTec final payment). If Q3 margin stays near 20% it caps the quality of a revenue beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-11 a margin decline alongside a revenue beat produced +0.68%, so margin has not been punished hard.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public. What is not known is whether the hardware pass-through continues in Q3. SciTec reported a FORGE operational milestone on 2026-10-28, which suggests continued program activity.

baseline_tension: Mixed: the beat and the possible licence-driven guide raise agree with the upside-paid skew and the run-up, so they are mostly priced; the negatives (sell-the-news, unlocked supply, Alpha slip) cut against the skew and are sized small for that reason and for the crowded short.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar unsourced or disputed): the Q3 consensus is $106.3M against a second listing of $114.56M, so the revenue-beat finding was cut from +1.0 to +0.5 and print_vs_bar from +6 to +5.
Rule 5 (an inference is filed small): the licence-driven guide raise rests on my own ASC 606 reading with no filing, so it was cut from +1.0 to +0.7 with the wide range kept.
Rule 9 (a segment finding net of the rest): the Alpha slip falls on the roughly 8% launch segment while spacecraft is booked, so it was cut from -1.0 to -0.7.
Rule 7 (crowded short, skew): this was already applied in the draft run-up finding (-1.5) and was not applied twice.
